pr_title: network: introduce an online state that respects RequiredForOnline=
pr_body:
resolves #19143

This PR adds a new "online" state to systemd-networkd which indicates whether a link is online based on the `RequiredForOnline=` property. Moreover, it exposes an overall "online" state through the networkd manager which is a survey the online state of all "required for online" links. Finally, it updates the `network_is_online()` utility function to make use of this state if it is meaningful. More detail can be found in the commit messages.

The motivation behind this change is to give a more meaningful online status to timesyncd - the only user of `network_is_online()`. An administrator can then configure `RequiredForOnline=no` on links which do not provide any gateway access, which prevents timesyncd from attempting spurious timesyncs when such links enter a degraded or routable state. This in turn makes for a faster timesync when a suitable link later comes online, as we have not exhausted timesyncd's internal rate limiter meanwhile. A detailed description of the problem is in #19143.
pr_comments:
Changes:
- remove `LINK_ONLINE_STATE_UNKNOWN` and use `_LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID` instead
- only compute online state for managed links with `RequiredForOnline=yes`
- fix a bug in the calculation of manager online state, and in general make it easier to read
- update documentation ever so slightly
- update networkctl to display online state for links/manager

The only significant change here is that I don't bother to compute an online state for links where `RequiredForOnline=no`. I think this is fair enough because for such links, we would fall back to the `LINK_OPERSTATE_RANGE_DEFAULT` range anyway, which could be potentially misleading. If a user sets `RequiredForOnline=no`, then the online state is useless anyway.

I think this fine for another review.

Something else to think about: Perhaps there is room for a networkd.conf `[Link]` option `AnyForOnline=` (or similar), which will set the manager online state to `online` in case any required link is online. A bit like the `--any` switch for systemd-networkd-wait-online. If false, then the state would be `partial` as is the case at the moment.

I haven't touched the wait-online code here, but with such a `AnyForOnline=` option for networkd, maybe most of the extra switches to the wait-online program can be removed and the service simplified to just wait on the overall manager online state. At the moment it does a lot of careful checking but I do wonder what the advantage of this is, when the administrator could just configure the same ranges and preferences in the .network files?

Anyway, those are just some personal thoughts of mine. The current PR doesn't affect wait-online in any way, nor was that the original aim.

As far as this PR is concerned, the advantage of a per-link online state is better visibility for the administrator. For example, a misconfigured system might have manager state "partial" when the expected state is "online", but without a per-link online state it can be a little tricky to identify the offline link(s) responsible for this. With the way I have implemented it right now, the administrator can just run `networkctl` and inspect all the "offline" links to narrow down the problem. This is another example of why I think it's good to distinguish between "unknown" and "offline" states for unmanaged/managed links.

@craftyguy Without container, I usually do something like the following to test networkd and networkctl from current git HEAD.
```
$ mkdir ~/git
$ cd ~/git
$ git clone https://github.com/systemd/systemd
$ cd systemd
$ git remote add sipraga git@github.com:sipraga/systemd.git
$ git fetch sipraga online-if-required
$ git checkout online-if-required
$ sudo mkdir /var/build/systemd
$ sudo chown USER:GROUP /var/build/systemd
$ cd /var/build/systemd
$ meson ~/git/systemd .
$ ninja
$ sudo systemctl edit systemd-networkd.service
$ cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/var/build/systemd/systemd-networkd
$ sudo systemctl restart systemd-networkd.service
$ /var/build/systemd/networkctl status --json
```
Of course, you can also use mkosi or something similar to create a container or vm instead.

issue_context.title: timesyncd may try to sync when system is not really online
issue_context.body:
I originally [posted about this on the systemd-devel mailing](https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/systemd-devel/2021-March/046239.html) list hoping to get some feedback on this problem. Below is more or less a repost, in the hopes of catching some more attention. In the absence of any other opinions, I will prepare a PR according to suggestion (2) below.

Thanks in advance!


**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
systemd-timesyncd listens for changes in network state and will start a timesync when it determines that the system is online. It does this via `network_is_online()`, which just queries the global carrier and address state advertised by systemd-networkd.

systemd-networkd determines the global carrier and address state by simply iterating through all links and taking the maximum of the link carrier and address states.

However, a routable link does not necessarily mean that the system is online. One example is with wireless access point interfaces: an AP is set up with hostapd and networkd configures a static IP address on that interface, making it routable. By the above, this causes timesyncd to attempt a timesync that is doomed to fail.

We are having trouble with this logic because we start hitting timesyncd's internal rate limiter. After a non-AP interface gets an IP and we are truly "online", timesyncd will try to start a timesync, but may defer it for up to 30 seconds due to rate limiting.

Ideally, timesyncd should be able to distinguish between the two cases such that it can ignore the state of the AP interface and avoid spurious timesync attempts.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Here are some proposals:


1. Add a new `[Link]` option `NotForOnline=` (or similar) to systemd.networkd(5) to indicate that this link being routable does not 
imply that the system is online. This could also implicitly set `RequiredForOnline=no` if desired. Then parse the option in `network_is_online()` to exclude certain links.

2. Add a new `[Link]` option `IgnoreLinkState=` (or similar) to systemd.network(5) to indicate to systemd-networkd that this link's 
carrier and address state should not be factored into the calculation of global carrier and address state.

3. Same as (1) above, but rather than adding a new option, just parse `RequiredForOnline=`.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Our current workaround is to restart systemd-timesyncd to force an immediate timesync, but this is an awful hack. Another workaround is to put systemd-timesyncd after `network-online.target`.

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**
v246. I believe the problem is also present in the main branch as of writing.
comments:
well, there are a myriad of reasons why connectivity might not be there. i mean, there's a long chain of routers usually towards reaching the internet, and any of those can fail. We use the carrier check as a reason to recheck, and we'll alwas retry after a while. 30s shouldn't be that bad...

I mean, we can certainly polish things further, but it's not really a bug here...

Wouldn't it suffice to make network_is_online() honour RequiredForOnline=? i.e. why another option?

Sure, I also think it's reasonable to just honour RequiredForOnline= in network_is_online().

Here's a quick attempt at doing that: https://github.com/sipraga/systemd/commit/cce3dd298266d39d615db3ba2ba7a95995390d80

I haven't made a PR because it still requires an update to the documentation for RequiredForOnline=, and I haven't tested it just yet. But does it seem like a reasonable approach?
This should probably be implemented networkd-side, not client-side

review_comments: This should be also initialized with `_LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID` in `manager_new()`.
Not a matter, but I prefer to add a blank line before `table_add_many()`.

Hmm, I think we should also set online state for unmanaged links.
How about the following?
```
if (operstate >= link->network ? link->network->required_operstate_for_online.min : LINK_OPERSTATE_RANGE_DEFAULT.min &&
    operstate <= link->network ? link->network->required_operstate_for_online.max : LINK_OPERSTATE_RANGE_DEFAULT.max)
        online_state = LINK_ONLINE_STATE_ONLINE;
else
        online_state = LINK_ONLINE_STATE_OFFLINE;
```

Hmm, what value would that bring? For unmanaged links, `LINK_OPERSTATE_RANGE_DEFAULT` is only a best guess on the part of networkd, since it does not know how the link should be configured. But it can be potentially misleading too. Why not be transparent about it?

For managed links where `RequiredForOffline=no`, I would argue the same way. By setting `=no`, the admin has no way to configure the actual `required_operstate_for_online`, so it will be a best guess.

I can of course do what you suggest - I don't think it's wrong per se - but I invite you to reconsider first.
I do not think this is necessary.

I put this here for managed links which have no carrier at boot. `link_update_operstate()` needs to get called at least once after the `link->network` pointer has been set, so that the online state can transition from `_LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID` to `LINK_ONLINE_STATE_OFFLINE`.

Put another way, we want managed links which are offline to be marked as such. Without this line, such links which never have carrier may be marked as "n/a" (or "unknown", etc.).

I'm not sure I see an alternative, except to have the default online state of a link be `LINK_ONLINE_STATE_OFFLINE`. But I am trying to make networkd as transparent as possible when it advertises the online state. Hence I prefer to say "networkd has no idea", than "networkd thinks this is offline".
hmm, do we really want both LINK_ONLINE_STATE_UNKNOWN and _LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID? The latter should suffice as marker for "dont know", no?

the intent here was to make it a "first class citizen" among statuses - it seems a little weird to repurpose _LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID for that. I'll try to change it in the next revision and we can see how it looks
I removed the unknown state and use _LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID now. Seems to work just fine.

Please add one more condition about unmanaged.
```
if (!link->network || link->network->unmanaged || !link->network->required_for_online)
```
I think, it is better to initialize this with `_LINK_ONLINE_STATE_INVALID` in `link_new()`.
